title: Clean Core Levels A–D for SAP Report Design (Beginner Guide)
introduction:
This guide explains SAP's Clean Core levels A–D for designing Reports in S/4HANA ↔ BTP projects with clear details, analogies, tools, examples, and best practices.

🔍 Why Clean Core?

  • Clean Core = designing SAP reports without modifying standard SAP tables or code.
  • Why? Ensures SAP upgrades don't break your reports.
  • How? Use SAP-approved APIs instead of direct table access.
apiExplanation:
📖 What is an API in SAP?

  • API (Application Programming Interface) = a safe door SAP gives you to get data without breaking walls.
  • Non-API = directly reading internal tables like EKKO, EKPO, or MARA (like picking locks on doors SAP didn't give you keys to).
  • Released API = officially supported by SAP (published in API Hub or CDS View Browser).

designGuidance:
1. Start with Level A
    • Search for released CDS views or OData services in the API Hub.
    • Build Fiori Elements or RAP apps instead of ALV.
    • Use BTP for side-by-side reporting (e.g., SAP Analytics Cloud).
  2. Use Level B only if A is unavailable
    • If no released CDS exists, use classic BAPI/RFC.
    • Document all dependencies and plan a roadmap to Level A.
  3. Treat Level C as technical debt
    • Direct table access works, but it's fragile.
    • Document all internal tables used and schedule remediation.
  4. Prohibit Level D for new reports
    • No modifications to standard SAP reports.
    • Establish governance: peer reviews + transport checks.

    • Do not modify standard workflow runtime/templates.
    • Enforce transport governance and code reviews to catch violations.
